title: Software
text:
Tools I have written or contributed to for analysing bacterial growth in plate readers, microfluidic chambers and bioreactors. Linked cards open the repository on GitHub. Cards marked private are not yet published.







FriendChip


Private repository

image analysis

microfluidics

author



From a raw .lif/.nd2 microfluidics timelapse to single-cell growth rates, dose–response fits and cross-feeding maps. One config per experiment, one CLI, GPU segmentation and tracking.









plate-functions


Private repository



R

growth curves

plate reader

author



R functions for 96-well plate-reader growth curves: log-linear sliding-window maximum growth rate, per-well yield / AUC / lag / carrying capacity, blank correction, time-grid sanity checks and per-plate parameter diagnostics. Shared as a git submodule across several lab projects.

Fork of the open-source ChiBio bioreactor platform with additions for OD dilution-series calibration, timed dosing schedules, fluorescence-assisted OD control and measurement-mutex fixes for the device’s read/write sequences.

title: Constantinos Xenophontos
text:
How bacteria grow, cooperate and cheat, and how those interactions change the way populations respond to antibiotics.
I am a microbial ecologist and postdoctoral researcher in Gabriele Micali’s Microbial Ecology Lab at IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital in Milan. I work with small synthetic bacterial communities, asking how cross-feeding, public goods and cheating shape their composition, and what those interactions do to antibiotic tolerance.
I run growth experiments in plate readers, microfluidic chambers and continuous-culture bioreactors, and I write the analysis pipelines that turn those time series into growth rates, lineages and dose–response curves. The code is on the Software page.
I did my doctoral research in microbial ecology at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv), where I tested ecological theory with synthetic bacterial communities and models of public-goods cheating. Before that I trained in ecology and evolution at Imperial College London and in biology at the University of Hull.
